title: RetroChimera: predicting small-molecule synthesis
summary: Published in Nature, the method combines a Transformer model (R-SMILES 2) and a template-based graph model (NeuralLoc) through a learned vote. In blind tests with expert chemists, 90% of complete routes were accepted, compared with 20–50% for the component models or a baseline, and nine of ten difficult targets were solved. Evaluation covered only ten targets; one wrong prediction invalidates an entire route.

evidence.tested: Blind tests by PhD-level chemists rated individual steps and complete routes for ten difficult targets: 90% of RetroChimera routes were accepted, and nine of ten targets were solved, versus 20-50% for the component models or baseline.
evidence.unknown: The route-level evaluation covers only ten targets; one incorrect prediction invalidates a route; NeuralLoc is constrained on reactions outside its template library, and R-SMILES 2 may hallucinate.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble of a Transformer (R-SMILES 2) predicting precursors and a graph neural network (NeuralLoc) selecting templates, combined by a learned rank-dependent vote.
